stage1.impression: A warm, coherent night view down a long oak-and-terrazzo room through a shopfront, with good pools of light on the floor, the banquette wall and the back. It still reads as CG: the end wall is a flat slatted surface under a pale peach light strip that reads as a signage lightbox, every surface sits in the same orange-brown, and the rainbow of glowing spheres on the shelf and plinth looks like gumballs, not one hero object. As it stands a magazine would read it as a generic warm bar render, not a specific, well-made place.

blocking_9: The lantern must read at a glance as a freestanding lit oak box: its top, sides and foot separated from the ceiling, walls and floor by dark gaps and a visible foot line, not as a slatted end wall
The acrylic band must glow amber with depth across its fins (visible edge glow and a falloff), not a flat pale peach strip like a lightbox (now 226/183/161, dE2000 21.7 from amber)
Materials must separate in hue and value under the warm light: plaster, oak, terrazzo and quartzite all currently sit in one orange-brown
The street viewpoint must show the glass: a faint reflection of the street in the dark upper and side areas, so it reads as seen from the sidewalk
No dead-black masses in the foreground: the counter's front (median 4.5) and the window mullion cutting the left third
Saturated colour must come mainly from EARF's products as the hero, not spread evenly across a rainbow row of lamps (out of scope here, see below)

defects.what: Acrylic band reads as a flat pale peach lightbox: lum 191, RGB 226/183/161, range 38, no fin depth and no edge glow
No visible gap or edge between the lantern's top and the ceiling, so the box reads as a wall
Downlight hot spot on the top of the baffle, with a white glint on the band above it
Window mullion is a full-height black bar in the left third, splitting the frame
Ceiling is an empty black void (median 9) with bare pinpoint downlights; no plaster and no glass reflection
Textbook scalloped spot pattern on a plaster wall that has the same orange as the oak (RGB 66/42/24)
A row of Cores in seven saturated tints reads as a candy display
Purple and white Hemisphere pendants add a second saturated colour high in the frame
Terrazzo shows fine CG grain noise in the darker parts at 1:1

changes.problem: The amber band reads as a flat pale peach lightbox, not lit amber acrylic.

change.setting: the lantern's band: emission (colour and level)
change.to: 0.6 at about 1900 K amber, with the emitter set back behind the fins so each fin's polished edge catches it and the light falls off top to bottom

changes.expected: The band reads deep amber and glowing, with visible fin rhythm and brighter fin edges; it becomes the most saturated warm element at the end of the room.

changes.problem: The lantern does not separate from the ceiling, side walls and floor, so it reads as a slatted end wall instead of a freestanding box.

evidence.measured: the ceiling above the band is near black (frame-top median 9), with no edge between the box top and the ceiling; the foot line is not visible at y about 555

change.setting: the lantern's foot line, plus a soft wash on the end and side walls behind and beside the box (the fill)
change.to: foot line 14.0; fill 0.25 W/m2, aimed so the plaster beyond the box's top and sides is lit a little more than the box's edges

changes.expected: A thin bright line under the box and a dim lit plaster gap around its top and sides, so the box's silhouette reads as an object.

changes.problem: All the materials sit in one orange-brown, so the plaster, oak and terrazzo do not read as different materials.

evidence.measured: plaster RGB median 66/42/24 against oak at the back of 141/80/43: the same hue

change.to: 2850 (keep the 2700 K sources warm but bring the lime plaster and terrazzo back toward warm grey)

changes.expected: The plaster reads as warm grey, the oak stays honey, and the amber band and the Ember pair stand out against them.

changes.problem: The counter's front is a dead-black mass in the foreground middle.

change.to: area 0.15 W/m2, 2700 K, low and grazing so the blackened steel shows its sheen and edge

changes.expected: The counter's face holds detail (soft sheen, a lit top edge) while staying the darkest object.

changes.problem: The window mullion cuts a full-height black bar through the left third, splitting the shop from the bar.

evidence.measured: a near-black vertical band 40 px wide at x about 320 to 355

change.to: shift sideways about 0.4 m so the mullion falls within 5 % of the left edge (or exactly on the shelf's edge), same target and lens

changes.expected: One uninterrupted view through the glass, with the lantern near the centre-right third.

changes.problem: Nothing shows the glass, so the street viewpoint does not read.

evidence.measured: lum_median 9, p95 43: an empty void with no reflection at glass reflection 0.6

change.to: a sodium-warm street lamp and a cooler shopfront opposite, bright enough to put a 5 to 10 % ghost reflection into the upper and right dark areas; reflection stays 0.6

changes.expected: A faint reflection of the street over the dark ceiling and the right wall, so the frame reads as taken through a shopfront.

changes.problem: A downlight puts a hot spot on the top of the baffle and a glint on the band, which reads as a CG lightbox.

evidence.measured: a bright cone at about 565,265 under the band (baffle region p95 180, clip 0.11 %)

change.to: 1.4 W/m2, spread evenly across the full width from below, with the downlight above the baffle's centre dimmed or re-aimed off it

changes.expected: The slots read evenly with a soft falloff upward, and nothing hot under the band.

changes.problem: There is too little air to carry the light from the band and the spots.

evidence.measured: a hard black right up to the band edge; no bloom

changes.expected: A faint amber glow around the band and soft beams in the spots, with the shadows still holding.

out_of_scope.request: Reduce the seven saturated Core tints on the shelf and the purple Hemisphere pendant, so that one colour (the Ember pair, and the amber band) leads
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes EARF's products as placed, including the Cores and Hemispheres in their tints; only the owner can change what is on show

out_of_scope.request: Give the lantern a visible roof setback or reveal from the ceiling
out_of_scope.why: The lantern's size and place and the ceiling height are fixed architecture

out_of_scope.request: Make the Tropos pair visible from the street as the hero
out_of_scope.why: It is inside the lantern as placed; seeing it would need a change to the plan or the porch
